messages:
nina: Quick thread — we need a clear stance on proto schema stability vs fast iteration for internal APIs. Product wants to iterate fields rapidly; infra wants a stable contract for routing/quotas/telemetry. Thoughts?

sam: +1 we keep bumping into this. main pain: generated clients break across teams when fields are removed/renamed.

dan: Do we have metrics on how often schema changes are consumer-visible?

mira: Not formally tracked. Anecdotally, weekly tweaks during feature sprints.

kevin: Proposal: define two tiers of internal endpoints — "stable" (semver, strict codegen, gateway enforcement) and "experimental" (JSON-over-gateway, dynamic fields, faster drift). Gateway routes are labeled and policy-driven.

nina: I like tiers. Key question: where do quotas/telemetry live? If gateway enforces too much we lose fidelity for per-model/per-route cost signals.

sam: We can keep telemetry at the gateway but propagate original proto metadata downstream via headers: X-Proto-Version, X-Route-Tier, etc. That preserves signals and lets dedicated pods record accurate metrics.

dan: Are we ok with the gateway doing proto<->json shims for experimental endpoints? Performance impact?

kevin: Shim cost is small for typical control-plane requests but not for high-throughput generation endpoints. For heavy paths we should require native proto and typed clients. Experimental tier is for lower throughput admin/feature flags.

mira: Rolling schema changes — how do we do client rollouts? Codegen + canary + runtime negotiation?

sam: Runtime negotiation seems good: clients send Accept-Proto-Version header; server responds with supported set. Gateway can route to compatible backend variant.

nina: Can we avoid breaking client code when fields are added/removed? Backwards compatibility rules: additive-only for stable, deprecation window for removals with gateway-level warnings.

kevin: Add a build-time lint and schema-bot that comments on PRs: block removals from stable APIs unless a deprecation flag and timeline are present. schema-bot: will mention this in CI.

schema-bot: PR check failed: modifications include field renames in stable/api/v1/gen.proto — add deprecation entries or move to experimental.

dan: Nice. For quotas: mapping should be per-route, not per-proto-message. If we rely on proto fields for quota keys (e.g., tenant_id), we need to standardize field locations. Gateway can normalize (read tenant_id from multiple message types into header).

mira: That normalization also helps telemetry and cost attribution. We can emit consistent attributes to the observability pipeline.

sam: UX for rollouts: console should expose route tiers, current proto version, last change, and a quick way to mark a version canary. Also a preview diff for generated client impact.

nina: Agreed. Feature request: console shows a "schema compatibility score" that flags non-backwards-safe changes and highlights impacted clients.

kevin: Implementation notes: 1) maintain canonical proto repo with tags for stable/experimental. 2) codegen pipeline produces clients by tag. 3) gateway reads routing policy mapping routes -> {tier, proto-tag, quota-policy}. 4) schema-bot enforces PR rules.

dan: Edge case: third-party SDKs that bypass gateway (internal infra teams). Enforcement will need network policies or service mesh to ensure routing flows through the gateway.

mira: We should document migration patterns: quick rename -> add new field (deprecated alias) -> after deprecation window remove. Provide middleware snippets for common languages.

sam: Also add runtime fallback: if backend receives unknown field, it should ignore (proto already supports this), but clients should fail fast on missing required fields. Promote optional over required wherever possible for stable APIs.

kevin: Agree. One more: telemetry hooks — include a small proto annotation (xredwood.route_key) so gateway auto-extracts routing keys for quotas. That keeps proto authoring ergonomic.

nina: Ok actionable list?

kevin: 1) Draft RFC: "Tiered internal API strategy" with enforcement rules and migration playbook.
schema-bot: RFC draft created: https://go/rfcs/135 (auto)

dan: 2) Add schema-bot checks to CI (block removals from stable).
mira: 3) Console mockups for schema compatibility and canary toggles.
sam: 4) Gateway: add header propagation and proto->json shim for experimental tier.
nina: Great. I'll start the RFC and sync with product to lock tier definitions. If anyone wants to pair on the console mock, ping me. :thumbsup:

kevin: thanks — this should reduce churn and make quotas/telemetry more reliable.

sam: one final note: keep an escape hatch — if an emergency removal is necessary, allow a fast-path but require posthoc deprecation plan and owner signoff.

nina: Cool — closing loop. We'll aim to present to platform council on Wed.
